Let me go through each example systematically:

## Example 1 (2024-10-01)

History shows prices generally trending UP from low 60s to high 65s:
- Start of period: 62.82, 63.39, 64.10, 63.87 (around Oct 1-9)
- End of period: 66.12, 65.56 (Oct 25-26)

The model forecasts are consistently LOWER than true outcomes by about:
- At horizon 0: 63.68 vs 63.61 (slightly higher, negligible)
- At horizon 1: 62.81 vs 62.60 (model 0.21 higher)
- At horizon 5: 60.42 vs 60.29 (model 0.13 higher)
- At horizon 8: 64.67 vs 65.00 (model 0.33 lower - error)
- At horizon 12: 63.20 vs 62.98 (model 0.22 higher)
- At horizon 17: 66.31 vs 66.12 (model 0.19 higher)

Wait, let me look more carefully. The model forecasts appear to be somewhat below reality in many places but not consistently in one direction.

Looking at the pattern more carefully:

Example 1 - comparing model vs true:
- The model seems to under-predict the price increases in the latter half of the 30-day horizon
- Around days 18-25, the gap widens significantly (model is ~1-2 euros too low)


- Early horizons show minimal deviations, with model forecasts closely aligning with actual prices

I notice the discrepancies become more pronounced as the forecast horizon extends, suggesting the model struggles to capture future price movements accurately.

In Example 2, a clear divergence emerges between model predictions and true outcomes. The forecasts consistently underperform, with differences ranging from 0.25 to 2.50 euros. Notably, the model fails to anticipate price fluctuations, particularly in the latter half of the 30-day projection.
